issues.description: The problem statement uses a different method name style for the total-students method (get_total_number_of_students()) than the rest of the materials which use camelCase (getTotalNumberOfStudents()). This naming/signature inconsistency between the problem text and the UML/template/solution can confuse students about the exact method name/signature they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement use the same camelCase method name as the UML/template/solution: change get_total_number_of_students() to getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Ensure all references in the markdown and examples consistently use getTotalNumberOfStudents() to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement text uses the snake_case name get_total_number_of_students() for the method that returns the total number of students, while the UML and the provided solution use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). The template's TODO comment also references the camelCase method. This mismatch in identifier naming between the problem text and the UML/solution can confuse students about the exact method name to implement and may lead to failing automated checks that expect the camelCase name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement with the UML and solution by changing the textual method name to camelCase: getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Alternatively, explicitly state that students should use the camelCase method name as shown in the UML to avoid ambiguity.
